page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-48xCPU-512GB is a memory-optimized virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 48 physical cores and 48 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is configured with a shared CPU allocation and contains 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 10.67 GB per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates strong multi-threaded and instruction-heavy capabilities, though single-core performance is limited. The Passmark CPU score is strong, placing in the top 25% with 58184.07, supported by strong results in extended instructions, encryption, and physics tests. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is also strong at 375.9 GB/sec. Conversely, stress-ng single-core CPU performance is poor, falling into the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth and database operations perform in the average range, with Redis SET operations achieving 58.62 million operations per second and static web serving throughput reaching 26.19 GB/sec. Large-model LLM text generation is weak, with the 7B model generating 6.29 tokens per second.

Given the shared CPU allocation and high memory density, this server offers a cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive workloads that can tolerate shared CPU resources. The high memory capacity of 512.0 GB makes it suitable for large-scale caching layers, in-memory databases, and multi-threaded data processing tasks. However, the poor single-core performance and lack of local storage make it less suitable for latency-sensitive single-threaded applications or high-I/O storage-heavy workloads without external storage attachments.
